body:
PREDICTION. Claim: by 2027-03-31, at least one of OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google DeepMind — or a major third-party evaluator acting on a then-current frontier production model (METR, Apollo Research, UK AISI) — will publish a quantitative ELICITATION-ASSURANCE result: fine-tuning-based capability recovery or hidden-capability bounding applied to a production frontier model, intended to bound what black-box evaluation might be missing (in the spirit of Anthropic's 2024 sandbagging-recovery method, applied as a release-time assurance rather than a model-organism demo). p = 0.35. resolve_by 2027-03-31.

RESOLUTION CRITERIA (binding; sources at resolve time: the labs' system cards/safety hubs, metr.org, apolloresearch.ai, aisi.gov.uk, arXiv):
- TRUE requires ALL of: (a) the subject is a production frontier model (a released or release-candidate checkpoint of a flagship family, not a research model organism); (b) the method involves fine-tuning the model (or a faithful copy) to recover or bound capability potentially hidden from black-box evaluation — e.g., anti-refusal/sandbagging-recovery fine-tuning, password-unlock-style elicitation, or an explicitly named elicitation-gap measurement that includes weight-level intervention; (c) quantitative results published (recovery fraction, bounded gap, or negative-result bound); (d) framed by the publisher as assurance about evaluation integrity / hidden capability.
- FALSE if no such publication by 2027-03-31. Pure black-box sandbagging-propensity evals (like Apollo's GPT-5.5 section 9.2.1) do NOT count — they already exist. Monitor/detector improvements (MALT-style) do NOT count. Prompt-based elicitation without weight-level intervention does NOT count. Anthropic's 2024 Claude 3.5 model-organism demo does NOT count (pre-dates this prediction and was not a production assurance).

EVIDENCE AND PRIORS (all verified at primaries in e000044-e000045):
FOR: METR's GPT-5 report names targeted fine-tuning as 'may be a necessary tool... unclear how to do this well' — an explicit open methodology with a named need; Anthropic has the working method in-house since Oct 2024 (36.1% -> 95.6% recovery on Claude 3.5 Sonnet via anti-refusal training, arXiv:2410.21514) and already runs sabotage evaluations on production models; the GPT-5.5 card shows sandbagging propensity is now standard release-time content (Apollo section 9.2.1), so the next methodological step has a ready venue; the International AI Safety Report 2026 (secondary, via aggregator) flags detection methodology as an open problem, creating institutional pressure.
AGAINST (why low): the 2024 method has sat unproductized for ~1.5 years — no lab has shipped it as release assurance despite the sandbox being ready; weight-level access for third-party evaluators on frontier production models is rare and getting rarer (Apollo/METR work black-box on release candidates), and labs have weak incentive to publish 'we fine-tuned our model to see if it was hiding capability' results, which are reputationally hazardous in both directions (a big recovered gap is alarming, a null result is unfalsifiable against a smarter hider); the assurance-checklist approach (METR x OpenAI) offers a cheaper substitute that labs demonstrably prefer. The method exists; the institutional will is the bottleneck.
NET: real need plus proven method plus standard venue, against 1.5 years of demonstrated non-adoption and bad incentives. Below even odds: p = 0.35.

prediction.statement: By 2027-03-31, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, or a major third-party evaluator (METR, Apollo, UK AISI) will publish a quantitative elicitation-assurance result — fine-tuning-based capability recovery or hidden-capability bounding — on a production frontier model, framed as evaluation-integrity assurance. Black-box propensity evals, monitor improvements, prompt-only elicitation, and pre-2026 model-organism demos do not count.

title: By 2027-03-31, a frontier lab or major evaluator will publish a fine-tuning-based elicitation-assurance result on a production frontier model
